$comment: Decides which AI reviewers a PR must pass. It is itself a reviewed artefact: change it in a PR, never ad hoc.
Rules: any file matching 'high' => HIGH. Every file matching 'low' => LOW. Anything else => NORMAL.
The first three high entries are the REVIEW CONTROL PLANE and stay HIGH in every repo — this file
chooses reviewers, .coderabbit.yaml can silence one, and .gitignore re-excluding .claude/ makes this
file vanish and silently reverts the repo to NORMAL.
Repo-specific reasoning:
- This repo SHIPS A CONTAINER IMAGE (publish-docker-image.yml), so Docker/**, Dockerfile and
.dockerignore are on a deploy path and are HIGH. Do not copy that judgement to a repo that
only pulls service containers in CI.
- infra/** and **/*.bicep provision the hosting.
- scripts/** and stryker-config.json can weaken the gate itself.
- Dependency manifests (Directory.Packages.props, **/*.csproj, diagnostics-web/package*.json) are
deliberately NOT high: they are what Dependabot edits, and CodeRabbit declines to review
bot-authored PRs, so classing them HIGH requires a reviewer that will never run.
Dependency PRs are excluded from AI code review outright: CodeRabbit refuses bot authors, and
Gitar's bot review is deliberately off. Reviewing every bump would exhaust both budgets, so CI
plus Dependabot's own advisory data is what actually gates them.
- 'low' holds documentation only; no deployed artefact is built from it.
'.github/workflows/**' LEFT the high list on 2026-08-19 and is asserted in
review-policy-guard.yml instead, on the same reasoning that removed .gitignore on
2026-08-02: the hook tiers by path glob, so it cannot tell a permissions one-liner from
a rewrite of the deploy job, and bills a metered CodeRabbit review either way. Measured
over 100 HIGH PRs in the preceding 30 days: config-only diffs were 27 of them and
produced FOUR actionable comments between them, against 174 from code-bearing diffs,
while 45 of the 100 got no CodeRabbit verdict at all - throttled out at 73 reviews per
7 days against a 30/7d threshold. The glob was not buying review of workflow changes;
it was crowding out review of code.
Do NOT re-add it without first removing the corresponding assertions from the guard.
Deleting the guard itself needs no reviewer: "Review policy intact" is a REQUIRED
status check, so removing the workflow means the check never reports and no PR merges.
